answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor identities to cryo-acoustic telemetry. A node authenticates by measuring seismic shifts across a glacier and signing readings with a lightweight cipher. Because micro-tremors from a gale yield unique spatial phase signatures, an attacker must deploy dedicated geophone sensors per identity, incurring substantial hardware and deployment costs. However, sudden ice fractures distort baseline propagation, causing occasional false rejections.
